source: National Survey of Family Growth 2002 (Cycle 6), female respondent public-use file (NCHS); women aged 15-44 interviewed 2002-03, first marriages begun 1970-2003
target: Annual rate of first-marriage dissolution (divorce, annulment or separation) per marriage-year from the wedding day; widowhood censored (Poisson rate, not a probability)
population: U.S. household population of women 15-44 in their FIRST marriage, husbands of any marital history; the wife's own report
weights: NSFG final weights (normalised to mean 1) times exposure

inputs.marriage_years: completed years since the wedding at the start of the year being scored (0 = first year)
inputs.wife_age_at_marriage: wife's age in years on the wedding day
inputs.husband_age_at_marriage: husband's age in years on the wedding day (wife's report)
inputs.wedding_year: calendar year of the wedding; outside 1970-2003 is extrapolation, so the app should hold it at the latest year in support and say so
inputs.husband_prior_children: Yes/No: husband had children from a prior relationship
inputs.wife_race_ethnicity: Hispanic, White, Black, Other (non-Hispanic unless Hispanic)
inputs.same_race_ethnicity: Same/Different: husband's broad race-ethnicity group versus the wife's
inputs.wife_intact_family: Yes/No: wife lived with both parents from birth to 18

abstain: wife previously married (only first marriages of women are in the data)
any partner outside the age-at-marriage support
note: Same data, target, folds and inputs as nsfg2002_first_marriage.json; a different set of model families. The logistic and naive Bayes models give a probability per marriage-year, converted to a rate as -log(1-p).
